cases.name: auth-valid-signature-passes
cases.description: A correctly signed request to an anonymous route succeeds. The positive case: every failure case below is only meaningful if this one is green.

cases.name: auth-valid-signature-with-signed-header-passes
cases.description: Signing a header the request carries is accepted.

cases.name: auth-disabled-key-is-unknown
cases.description: A disabled key authenticates like a nonexistent one; the response does not distinguish them.

cases.name: auth-clock-skew-ahead
cases.description: A timestamp an hour ahead of the server is outside the default window.

cases.name: auth-clock-skew-behind
cases.description: A timestamp an hour behind the server is outside the default window too.

cases.name: auth-missing-signed-header
cases.description: The signed-headers list names a header the request does not carry.

cases.name: auth-foreign-scheme-is-malformed
cases.description: An Authorization header with a scheme this server does not speak is a syntax fault, stage 1, not an authentication fault.

cases.name: auth-signature-over-wrong-path-fails
cases.description: A signature computed for one path does not authorize another. The runner signs for the path it sends, so this is provoked with a corrupt signature on a non-trivial path.

cases.name: presign-valid-passes
cases.description: A presigned URL for an anonymous route is accepted.

cases.name: presign-expired
cases.description: An expiry in the past is rejected with its own code so clients can tell it from a bad signature.

cases.name: presign-too-long
cases.description: An expiry further ahead than the server's maximum lifetime (default 7 days) is rejected.

cases.name: presign-disabled-key-is-unknown
cases.description: Presigned URLs are verified against the key as it is now; a disabled key fails every URL it signed.
